> Original strategy notes (user-directed, now folded into the ranking above):
> - **CONTEXT RAILS (model-per-stream reservation):** reserve a model (or endpoint slot) exclusively for a task
>   stream/epic — one card's whole lifecycle (worker turns, re-drives, bounces) stays on ONE warm model whose KV
>   cache never sees a foreign prompt; other models serve other streams. The scheduler allocates rails, not turns.
> - **SINGLE-CARD FAN-OUT as the parallelism mode:** when the fleet can't give every active card its own rail,
>   PREFER fanning multiple models out on ONE card (worker + reviewer + critic + best-of-N attempts pipelined on
>   the same content) over running unrelated cards in parallel — cross-card interleaving is what thrashes every
>   cache; same-card fan-out shares most of its context by construction. Real card-parallelism only when enough
>   models/pools exist to give each card a rail ("don't start what you can't keep warm").
> - **MY OWN ANALYSIS (pre-research, to be validated):** the fleet is memory-bandwidth-bound — prefill and decode
>   compete for the same bandwidth, so a cold 20k-token prefill (~seconds of full-bandwidth burn) can cost MORE
>   aggregate throughput than the parallelism it buys; expected-prefill belongs IN the routing cost function
>   (prefillTokens × missLikelihood ÷ prefillSpeed vs decode gain). Cache warmth is a per-(endpoint, promptShell)
>   property the scheduler can TRACK deterministically (we know every prompt we send — compute the shared-prefix
>   length against the endpoint's last prompt, no probing needed: a "warmth ledger"). Rails then fall out naturally:
>   route to maximize predicted prefix reuse, subject to the diversity constraints for DECISION roles (reviewer/
>   critic must stay lineage-diverse — rails must never silently sacrifice §5.AB diversity; a diverse decision turn
>   is a legitimate cache miss, budget it as such).
> - **MULTI-PROJECT PARALLELISM → LATE (user decision 2026-07-02):** running multiple projects in parallel on one
>   fleet dilutes every cache and rail; DEPRIORITIZE enabling/optimizing it until the single-project cache/rail
>   design is proven (ties to the existing multi-workspace meta-chat FUTURE note — same lane).
> **Vision (user, 2026-06-29):** a user-facing **"sysprompt size" setting** with **4–5+ levels**, PLUS an **auto** mode that
> adjusts sys-prompt depth to (a) the actually-available context window and (b) the context the TASK needs, PLUS intent
> modes: **"minimize"** vs **"balance prompt + task info"** vs **"max actual task information"**. !Klein must **NEVER waste
> context space** — it matters for processing SPEED, processing QUALITY, and how much SMALL machines can still do. Also:
> deeply research keeping context overhead minimal + best use of **LM Studio / MLX prompt-CACHING** so the prompt-processing
> experience is best-possible while still targeting best-quality prompts. AND: **!Klein itself must waste NO system
> resources** — RAM, CPU, Disk, GPU, VRAM — deeply optimized for all.
>
> **RESEARCH SYNTHESIS (2026-06-29, 4 opus passes — see [[context-economy-research]]). Three prompt-economy pillars that
> all point the SAME way, plus the resource mandate:**
> 1. **LEAN + JIT + MODULAR (quality).** "Smallest set of HIGH-SIGNAL tokens" (Anthropic). Minimal ≠ short — *no token
>    without purpose*; **bloat actively DEGRADES quality** (attention dilution / context-rot / lost-in-the-middle), not
>    just cost. The biggest structural lever is **progressive disclosure / just-in-time**: keep only name+description
>    resident, load the rest on demand (exactly the §5.AE skill-set + §5.O tool-card direction). Claude Code itself is
>    110+ **conditionally-assembled** instructions where only relevant sections load → validates a LEVELED/conditional
>    sysprompt. Techniques: examples > exhaustive rules; tool-description response-format enums (Anthropic 206→72 tok);
>    strip filler.
> 2. **CACHE-AWARE LAYOUT (speed) — the new, high-impact finding.** llama.cpp / LM Studio / MLX all use **automatic prefix
>    KV-caching keyed on EXACT BYTE-equality** (no manual cache_control). So: a **byte-identical STABLE PREFIX** (system
>    prompt + tool defs) reused every turn, with ALL volatile content (date, RAG, task, turns) appended AFTER. One changed
>    byte in the prefix ⇒ full re-prefill (**~200 ms cached vs 30–120 s uncached**, up to 93% TTFT loss). **CRITICAL:
>    injecting today's date into the system prompt — the §5.AC behavior that spawned §5.AE — silently DEFEATS caching.**
>    Caveats: hybrid-attention models (Qwen3.5/Gemma3/GPT-OSS, SWA/Mamba) SILENTLY disable prefix reuse in LM Studio + MLX
>    → verify per-model via `cached_tokens`; MLX has file-persisted prompt caches for a warm prefix. **Operational reality
>    (user 2026-06-29, LM Studio #1697): caching FAILS SILENTLY and is engine/format-specific** (MLX GPT-OSS-20B broken,
>    GGUF of the same model fine) — and the orchestrator's OWN request construction is often the culprit (openclaw #19892:
>    a "Current time:" line in the system prompt wiped the cache every turn, 40k context 5s→200s). So !Klein must DETECT
>    cache health per (engine×model×format) and ADAPT — see item E. And the target is not just caching but **best
>    speed+correctness+completeness+QUALITY on EVERY request** since compute is the small-HW bottleneck — see item H.
> 3. **COMPACTION/PRUNING, NOT TOKEN-COMPRESSION (small-model-safe).** For LOCAL small models, query-agnostic token
>    compression (LLMLingua) + truncation HURT weak models most (truncation → 74–96% task collapse) and the compressor
>    itself costs wall-clock (~5× slower on M1 than A100) — it's a *fit-more-context / RAG-noise-removal* tool, NOT a local
>    latency play. The local wins: **summarization compaction + tool-result clearing** for long agent loops (mandatory once
>    history > window; preserve decisions/bugs/state, drop raw tool output) and **query-aware pruning (Provence, a 0.4B
>    DeBERTa that runs locally, 50–80% cut at ≈0 loss, near-free when fused with a reranker)** for RAG.
>
> **The convergence:** a LEVELED, MODULAR system prompt that stays a byte-stable cacheable PREFIX and loads task detail JIT
> is simultaneously leaner (quality), faster (cache hits), and smaller-machine-friendly — all three user goals from ONE
> design. Ties §5.AD (smart-zone + learned budget), §5.AE (dynamics levels), §5.AB (context-window clamp), §5.AF (ledger).
>
> **EMPIRICAL JUSTIFICATION (why this matters most on small machines).** Effective context ≪ advertised (RULER: GPT-4
> 128K→~64K effective; many ≥32K-claimed models hold baseline only to ~16K). Length ALONE degrades quality even with
> PERFECT retrieval, and **small/open models collapse hardest** — up to **85%** loss from length alone (arXiv 2510.05381),
> NoLiMa: Llama-70B 97%→43% at 32K. Middle-buried info can be WORSE than no context (Lost-in-the-Middle: 56.1% closed-book
> floor); a SINGLE irrelevant sentence costs ~22 pts (GSM-IC); even "repeat the words" rots past a few thousand tokens
> (Chroma Context Rot). Fixed sysprompt overhead is real: Claude Code ~14.3k tok, Cline ~11.7k, Cursor ~5k — on a 32k local
> window a 14k prompt is ~44% gone BEFORE the task. **PRIOR ART:** no shipped agent exposes a sysprompt-DEPTH ladder
> (Aider tiers by model/edit-format, Cursor Max-Mode by window, Agent Skills by relevance) — the exact feature is only a
> Cline feature-REQUEST (#1310/#2889) → genuinely novel. Best models to borrow: Agent-Skills 3-level progressive
> disclosure (~30-80 tok/skill at rest) for JIT, and RouteLLM (a cheap complexity classifier → 85% strong-model-call
> reduction at 95% quality) for AUTO selection. Guardrail (Anthropic + Aider): "minimal ≠ short" — dropping HIGH-SIGNAL
> content has measurable cost (Aider: removing "high-level diff" guidance → +30-50% edit errors); protect load-bearing
> instructions in EVERY level, and put the few non-negotiable rules at the TOP and BOTTOM (never mid-prompt).

### 5.AS — Orchestrator role: deep research + evaluate (adopt / strengthen / reject-with-reasons) *(2026-07-01, user — RESEARCH, not started)*
> **User ask (2026-07-01):** "deeply research and evaluate if an **orchestrator role** would be a good idea for !Klein. If we have that already covered, check how we can make it stronger; if it does not suit !Klein, document the reasoning; if it is a good idea, add detailed instructions how we can integrate this idea to !Klein's best and maximum benefit." So this cell's OUTPUT is a **decision + a plan or a documented rejection**, not code — do the research first (web + codebase), then write the verdict here (and, if adopt, the sequenced build).
>
> **What "orchestrator role" means here (frame before researching):** a dedicated COORDINATING agent/role that owns the *meta-loop* — decompose a goal → route each sub-task to the best-fit model/role → sequence + parallelize across the swarm → monitor progress/blockers → re-plan/re-route on failure → integrate results — as opposed to today's more *implicit/distributed* orchestration. Distinguish a **role** (a prompt/model-class assignment, like architect/worker/reviewer) from an **orchestration LAYER** (control-plane logic); the question spans both.
>
> **First: map what !Klein ALREADY has (is this covered?).** Honest inventory before proposing anything new — likely-overlapping pieces: the **§5.M chat agent loop** + **§5.0.1 autonomous goal-driven run** (plans a focus chain, drives turns to a goal); **§5.AB decomposition** (`decideCardDecomposition` / `build-decomposition-routing-candidates` — a goal → a DAG of cards routed to loaded models); **role-model-class.ts** (architect/worker/reviewer → model-class fit) + **swarm-roster** + **model-task-affinity**; the **auto-model-selection north-star** (`[[auto-model-selection-vision]]` — no manual role→model config; !Klein auto-picks best-fit per card); the **§5.AF durable scheduler** (unattended multi-card execution + restart); the **§5.AA robustness ladder** (force-advance, stall/loop detection); the **§5.K reviewer loop**. The board itself is arguably the orchestration substrate (cards = tasks, lanes = state, the swarm = workers). **Key question: is orchestration an emergent property of [decompose + auto-select + durable-schedule + board-state], or is there a real GAP a dedicated orchestrator would fill** (e.g. cross-card global planning, dynamic re-routing mid-run, dependency-aware parallelization, a single accountable "conductor" that adapts the plan as evidence arrives)?
>
> **✅ RESEARCHED + DECIDED — 2026-07-01 (multi-agent workflow: codebase inventory + 5 web-research angles → gap analysis → verdict → 3-lens adversarial verify; ALL 3 lenses confirmed `verdictHolds`).**
>
> **VERDICT: STRENGTHEN — wire the existing DETERMINISTIC orchestration cores; do NOT add an orchestrator SwarmRole or a central LLM "conductor."** Both meanings of "orchestrator role" are wrong for !Klein: an LLM conductor is the exact weak-orchestrator failure the research warns about for a *uniform local small-model swarm* (weak-orchestrator error amplification up to ~17× — even centralized ~4.4×; MAST system-design/misalignment failures ~42%/~37%; token/context blowup ~4.6–15× against the ≥32k floor; Cognition + Anthropic both find coding + high-interdependency is NOT a multi-agent fit; Anthropic's "cheap-orchestrator-wins" result assumes STRONG sub-agents — the opposite of our swarm). A NEW `decideOrchestrationStep` core would also **duplicate** cores that already exist. The orchestration "brain" must stay **deterministic (rules + catalog + ledger)** — and crucially, **most of it is already BUILT as pure/tested cores that are simply UNWIRED** (verified: zero runtime importers).
>
> **Inventory (what's LIVE):** decompose-goal→card-DAG (`decompose_project` → plan-artifact-apply → board), per-card auto-model-selection (`selectSwarmRouteForTask` wired at `start-task-session.ts`), architect/worker role pick (an implicit deterministic "supervisor-as-router" — the safe local shape the research endorses), reactive cross-card unblock + auto-start (`completeTaskAndGetReadyLinkedTaskIds` → `autoStartTaskIds`, file-overlap serialized), decompose stall/loop recovery (`DecompositionStallNudger`), the §5.0.1 single-run autonomous conductor (`runAutonomousChatAgent` + focus-chain — single-threaded, the research's preferred shape for coupled work), board-as-substrate, and the restart-surviving durable START-queue. *(Precision, per the duplication-lens critique: `coalescing-scheduler.ts` IS wired into `runtime-state-hub.ts` as a live event-coalescing throttle — correctly NOT counted as orchestration, because it's a throttle, not a scheduler.)*
>
> **The real GAPS = built-but-DARK cores (wire, don't invent):** `durable-scheduler.ts` + `durable-run-controller.ts`/`-ports`/`-registry` + `durable-scheduler-ledger.ts` + `durable-run-reaction.ts` + `durable-lease-renewal.ts` (mid-run crash recovery — a card actively running when the process dies is currently leaseless/lost); `durable-scheduler-ready-order.ts` (`orderReadyJobs`) + `durable-job-critical-path.ts` + `durable-scheduler-backpressure.ts` (contention: ready cards start in board order not critical-path order, per-endpoint queues unbounded); `adaptive-decomposition-decision.ts` (`decideCardDecomposition`) + `decomposition-redecompose-trigger.ts` (`decideRedecomposeAction`) — adaptive granularity + bounded re-planning, both pure/tested with **zero callers**. All confirmed UNWIRED (no `src/server`/`src/trpc` importers).
>
> **THE PLAN — deterministic control-loop WIRING (no LLM conductor); sequenced, measurement-gated.** *(These 7 STEPS are

### 5.AT — Board→chat feedback: the board as the chat's task-planning brain *(2026-07-01, user — ACTIVE, designed)*
> **Vision (user 2026-07-01):** make the kanban board **"basically the long-term task-planning brain of the chat."** The user mainly talks to the **CHAT**; the board reflects + organizes the main goal and how it decomposes to be worked by the agent swarm. The board = the *simplest, most intuitive way to control + interact with !Klein* — investigating/adapting/interacting with cards is possible, but the **main workflow is just the chat**; the board gives transparency + optional micro-management. **The MISSING piece is FEEDBACK from the board/cards BACK to the chat** (updates, results, details) so the user gets progress without leaving the conversation. **The hard part: don't SPAM the user while keeping it comprehensive, meaningful, complete.**
>
> **Confirmed gap (codebase-verified):** the connection is **one-way today** — the chat has board tools (chat→board: `get_board` read + create/start cards, `chat-board-tools.ts`), but the **chat session never observes task/board state** (no board→chat path). The seams to build it EXIST in-process.
>
> **✅ RESEARCHED + DESIGNED — 2026-07-01 (multi-agent workflow: codebase inventory + web research on agentic-platform feedback UX / notification-batching / interruption science / HITL loops + design + 3-lens adversarial verify). Sources: Devin, Claude Code background tasks (+ its #17456/#18544 "forced-turn" cautionary bugs), Cursor/Copilot/ChatGPT-Agent/Manus, LangGraph HITL.**
>
> **PRINCIPLES:** (1) **Anti-spam is the PRIMARY constraint** — default posture SUPPRESS; a board event earns a chat message only by clearing an explicit gate (the two-layer split every platform converges on: board = high-fidelity source of truth, chat = low-frequency channel). (2) **LOCAL-FIRST** — the only summarizer is the chat's own local model (`ChatModelDeps`); deterministic template is the floor/fallback, never cloud, never block. (3) **NEVER force a model turn** — append with `role:"system"` as a pure notification the model is NOT obligated to answer (the Claude Code "task completed (exit 0)" → wasteful "Great!" turn is the cautionary tale). (4) **NOTIFY vs ASK is a hard type split** — NOTIFY = FYI, batchable, silent-eligible; ASK = a real human decision-point (needs-input / unsafe-ack / held delivery gate) that surfaces promptly + never batches away. (5) **The BOARD IS THE INBOX** — reuse `collectOperatorInbox` (`operator-task-state.ts`); chat feedback is a POINTER into the board ("Card X needs you" + link), not a re-narration. (6) **STATE-TRANSITIONS not states** — diff prev vs new summary (the hub already does this at `runtime-state-hub.ts`); steady `running` produces nothing. (7) **Routing requires OWNERSHIP** — a card event reaches a chat session only if that session OWNS the workspace/goal; no owner ⇒ NOTHING (never broadcast to every open chat). (8) **Everything is a pure, tested verdict.**
>
> **EVENT→MESSAGE POLICY:** **ASK-tier (immediate, bypasses digest+quiet):** needs-input (`clarifyingQuestionPending` §5.S), unsafe-action ack (`awaitingHostActionAck` §5.M-G3b), delivery gate held (`deliveryGateHeld` §5.L), sandbox-unavailable block — each carries a suggested verb (approve/edit/reject/respond); map 1:1 to `classifyOperatorTaskState()==='risky'`. **NOTIFY-tier (prompt but coalescible):** DONE/ready-for-review (session→`awaiting_review` or card→review column; carry `latestHookActivity.finalMessage` = the agent's own result text), FAILED/interrupted, lost heartbeat. **Milestone-only (digest-preferred):** decomposition phase-boundary from `FocusChainSummary` (≤1 per card per window, NOT every step tick). **Silent/digest-only:** `nklein_team_progress` swarm narration (too frequent), coalesced 150ms ticks, running heartbeats, token usage, non-boundary checkpoints, →running/queued. **Suppress entirely:** any event whose owning session can't be resolved; a repeat of an already-surfaced unresolved `(taskId, signalKind)` (dedupe key, like `use-review-ready-notifications.ts`); any NOTIFY while the owning session is mid-autonomous-run (it sees board state through its own tools).
>
> **BATCHING/DIGEST:** back-off burst-coalescing is the DEFAULT for NOTIFY (first surfaces promptly; a burst within the window collapses to ONE digest) — reuse the EXISTING `createCoalescingScheduler` (`coalescing-scheduler.ts`, same primitive the hub uses) keyed per owning-session. Grouping = session→card; a burst renders as one rollup ("Card A ready for review, Card B failed, 2 progressing") capped first/last-N + "+M more (open board)". **ASK never batches** — it flushes any pending digest + delivers standalone. **While-you-were-away rollup:** track per-session `lastSeenAt`; away-events fold into ONE catch-up digest on return, ordered by PRIORITY (ASK on top) not chronology. **Optional LOCAL LLM rewrite** of the digest (template is the guaranteed fallback). Thresholds injectable/testable: back-off ~30–60s (scaled by low-power mode), card-line cap 5, milestone 1/card/window, ASK re-surface ≤1 per ~30 min.
>
> **USER CONTROLS:** per-session **verbosity** (default `concise`): SILENT (board-only, pure pull) · CONCISE (ASK + DONE/FAILED only) · NORMAL (+ milestones) · VERBOSE (+ periodic swarm-activity digest; still never raw team-progress). **Mute** per-card + per-session. **Quiet/DND** (queue NOTIFY, release as one batch on exit; ASK breaks through). **Pull-on-demand `get_board_status`** tool (always available — synchronously returns `summarizeWorkspaceBoardHealth` + inbox; the escape hatch that makes aggressive suppression safe; SAME digest builder as push). **Push toggle** (per-session `readyForReviewNotificationsEnabled`-style boolean, global default + per-session override). **Opt-in desktop/`PushNotification` escalation** for ASK-tier only (reuse `use-review-ready-notifications.ts` dedupe).
>
> **ARCHITECTURE / SEAMS (in-process — `chatService` + `runtimeStateHub` share the runtime, no IPC):** task-session `onSummary` (hub already taps it) → a new **`BoardChatFeedbackBridge`** that diffs prev/next, resolves the owning session, calls the pure decision core, schedules the per-session coalescer, and on flush builds the message + appends it + emits a live UI event. **Seam 1 — out-of-turn write:** REUSE the existing `chatService.appendMessage(sessionId, {role:"system", content})` (already present, no model turn — *do NOT add a new method*, per the arch-critique). **Seam 2 — session↔workspace ownership:** add `ChatSession.ownedWorkspaceId` (+ optional `trackedTaskIds`) with back-compat (`.optional()` + replay-normalize), stamped when a chat turn decomposes/creates cards into a workspace (`chat-agent-tool-deps-resolver.ts`); no owner ⇒ no feedback. **Seam 3 — live UI read (the hardest gap):** the sidebar chat only refetches its transcript on the user's turn (or a 2.5s autonomous poll) — a server-pushed system message sits unseen. Add a hub **`chat_message_appended`** event (mirror the existing `task_chat_message`) → client refetch of `chat.getTranscript` (fast); upgrade to a `chat.streamSession` subscription (mirror `chat.streamMessage`'s async-queue) later if needed.
>
> **BUILD (pure-core-first; each GREEN):**

Output verdict = { action: `suppress`|`surface_ask`|`surface_notify`|`defer_to_digest`, tier, signalKey, suggestedVerbs?, milestone? }. ### 5.AU — Epics/Streams above cards + multi-level chat addressing ("whose message is this?") *(2026-07-01, user — ACTIVE, designed)*
> **Vision (user 2026-07-01):** organize cards into higher-level **STREAMS/EPICS** that drive the user-facing updates in the MAIN CHAT and point the user to the detailed info streams (cards + their card-threads/outputs) when they want them — *"Claude background-task overview, but with even more detail inside."* The user mainly talks to the **main chat** (sees card outputs there) but can ALSO write into a specific card's thread to guide it. **The tricky part the user named: clarity about the exact TARGET of a main-chat message** (the goal / a stream / a specific card / an answer to a pending question). Builds directly on §5.AT (board→chat feedback).
>
> **✅ RESEARCHED + DESIGNED — 2026-07-01 (multi-agent workflow: codebase inventory + web research on hierarchical task-overview UX / message-addressing + reference-resolution / multi-agent message routing / notification rollup / focus-context UX + design + 3-lens adversarial verify). Sources: Devin/Claude-Code/Manus/Copilot-Workspace task trees, Linear/Jira/Shortcut epics, Slack threads+@mentions, LangGraph HITL routing.**
>
> **GROUNDING (codebase-verified — the seams EXIST):** the only grouping today is `generatedFromPlan.planSlug` (immutable provenance: cards from one decomposition share a slug) + `dependsOn`/`board.dependencies` DAG edges — **no Epic/Stream entity, no rollup**. Each card IS a per-card agent conversation (task session) with a full transcript; **a user CAN send into a specific card via `sendTaskSessionInput(taskId, text, mode)`** (wired `task-chat-send` → the service) — but only from that card's panel; the main chat has **no handle to route there**. The main-chat `ChatSession` is board-INDEPENDENT (has a `goal` string, NO card/stream link, **NO notion of a message target**) and drives the board only via `get_board`/`create_card`. Crucially, **reply-to-a-pending-question is HALF-BUILT**: the autonomous loop already models `request_user_input → needs_user → pause → resume-with-answer`, and §5.AT's `decideBoardChatFeedback` already emits ASK verdicts with a stable `signalKey=${taskId}:${kind}` — so the addressing model EXTENDS existing seams, it doesn't invent them.
>
> **THE MODEL — 4 tiers:** **Goal** (the chat session's existing `goal` — no new entity) → **Stream/Epic** (a NEW explicit named entity) → **Card** (a task) → **Card-thread** (the card's transcript). Main chat converses at Goal/Stream altitude (rollups up, guidance down); cards + their threads are the drill-in detail.
>
> **STREAM SEMANTICS:** a Stream is an **explicit, named entity SEEDED from derivation then persisted** — `deriveStreams` (pure core) proposes one stream per `generatedFromPlan.planSlug` (titled from the source card), falling back to `dependsOn`-connected components; membership is an **additive, back-compat `card.streamId?`** (same optional-CRDT pattern as `generatedFromPlan`, so old boards load unchanged), single-parent, **flat under the goal (no nesting in v1** — research: deep nesting is unnavigable for a low-attention local-first UX). Status = a **status-frontier roll-up** (`deriveStreamRollup`, pure): count-based progress (done/total, disclosed method — no story points), a health badge that goes `blocked/at_risk` when a member is ASK-blocked/heartbeat-lost even at high %, and explicit **`stale` vs `no-signal`** (never false-green). `RuntimeStream = { id, title, createdAt, updatedAt, source: decomposition|manual|dependency, planSlug?, archived? }` — **no denormalized counts** (rollup is always derived).
>
> **ADDRESSING LADDER (the crux) — a pure `resolveMessageTarget` core; deterministic-first, the LLM is the LAST rung only.** Target = `{ kind: answer|card|stream|goal, id?, pendingKey?, displayLabel, confidence, source }`. Order is load-bearing: **RUNG 1 explicit `@card:<id>`/`@stream:<id>`/`@<title-slug>`** (Slack @mention analogue; routes + subscribes). **RUNG 2 reply-binding to a pending ASK** — the killer seam: persist the session's outstanding ASKs (from §5.AT ASK verdicts) and bind a reply to one. *(Critique fix: bind deterministically when there is exactly one outstanding ASK **whose owning card is the current focus / last-referenced** — not "exactly one ASK on the whole board" — and add a light local `is-this-an-answer` intent check so a fresh unrelated instruction doesn't misbind.)* **RUNG 3 persistent visible focus** (`session.focus = {kind,id}`). **RUNG 4 default to the goal** (today's only behavior — now the explicit fallback). **RUNG 5 LLM disambiguator** — fires ONLY on genuine residual ambiguity (>1 slug match, >1 unbindable ASK, focus-set-but-reads-like-new-goal), returns a **pick among provided candidates, never a free-form route** (weak-model risk contained). **Target ALWAYS shown** (a persistent "talking to X" composer chip: `Goal` / `#Auth stream` / `card #42` / `answering: <ASK>`) and **ALWAYS overridable in one action** (the chip is a control; dismiss → back to Goal). A targeted message is **RELAYED, not re-answered in chat** — via the existing `sendTaskSessionInput` through a new thin `send_to_card`/`send_to_stream` tool. **COMMUNICATION ≠ EXECUTION (user 2026-07-01 — corrects the earlier "just start the card"):** relaying a message must NOT force-start a card that has blocking predecessors. Decouple the two: every message is durably delivered to the card's **mailbox** (always allowed), while **"card start" = begin WORK, and that stays readiness-gated** (the §5.AS dependency-unblock logic — never bypassed). The EFFECT of a message = `f(card state × intent)` via a pure `resolveCardMessageEffect` core: RUNNING ⇒ live guidance to the agent; READY ⇒ queue to mailbox (don't auto-start) or, for a clear "go", REQUEST a start (still gated); BLOCKED ⇒ queue to mailbox (waits with the card, consumed as opening context when it runs) — a *question* is answered from board/ledger STATE ("blocked by A, B") or a cheap read-only **CONSULT** turn, distinct from WORK; DONE ⇒ append a follow-up. **WORK vs CONSULT** is a hard split: WORK does the task (gated); CONSULT answers *about* the card (ungated, read-only, local-first — prefer state-derived answers, spend a model turn only for substantive questions). The mailbox is VISIBLE ("2 pending notes from you") and its landing is confirmed via §5.AT feedback. A steer to a BLOCKED card surfaces a gated **suggest-unblock** ("blocked by A — reprioritize / drop the dependency?"), never a silent queue and never an auto-unblock.
>
> **FEEDBACK ROLLUP BY STREAM (reuses §5.AT — no renderer change):** `buildBoardChatDigest`'s `groupLabel` IS this seam. The bridge takes the per-card `decideBoardChatFeedback` verdicts (unchanged), buckets them by owning `card.streamId`, and calls the digest per stream with the stream name + the `deriveStreamRollup` one-liner → *"Auth stream — 3 tasks progressed, 1 needs you"* with capped card-lines nested + "+M more". Tier semantics survive: **ASK is never batched away** (an ASK in any stream keeps that stream's digest prompt; `askCount` already exposed), NOTIFY/MILESTONE coalesce; **dedup before counting** (reuse `signalKey`/`alreadySurfacedKeys`) so at-least-once replays don't inflate "N progressed".
>
> **DRILL-IN UX:** a **persistent overview surface** (NOT buried in the transcript — the Claude-Code TodoWrite pain point): the goal-level stream list, one row per stream (title + health badge + progress + frontier "now: card #42"). **Three-click drill** reusing existing UI: stream row → the stream's cards as the existing dependency DAG (`decomposition-graph-view`) → a card → its thread (`card-detail-view`). A **breadcrumb** `Goal > #Auth stream > card #42 > thread` — the SAME string as the composer's "talking to" chip, so focus + location are one surface. Minimal-list/fetch-detail split (protect the ≥32k floor). Per-stream steer/cancel (not one global stop). Override the target from any depth.
>
> **ARCHITECTURE:** 3 NEW pure cores — `deriveStreams` (src/core/stream-derivation.ts), `deriveStreamRollup` (src/core/stream-rollup.ts), `resolveMessageTarget` (src/core/message-target-resolver.ts). A `RuntimeStream` entity + additive `card.streamId?` + `board.streams[]` (board-object CRDT, back-compat). REUSE `sendTaskSessionInput` for the relay (a new thin `send_to_card`/`send_to_stream` chat tool — do NOT build a new card-write path). Extend `ChatSession` with `focus?` + `outstandingAsks?` (additive, replay-normalized). Extend the §5.AT bridge to group by `streamId` + maintain `outstandingAsks` (add on ASK, clear on answer-relay). Extend the `sendMessage`/`runChatAgentTurn` front door with `resolveMessageTarget` (relay on card/answer/stream, run-goal otherwise, candidate-picker on `needsClarification`).
>
> **BUILD (pure-core-first; each GREEN). ✅ ALL PURE CORES + DATA/SCHEMA LAYER SHIPPED (2026-07-01, commits e3911036..45a49209) — remaining is live runtime/chat/UI WIRING:**

### 5.AV — Valid-task-graph-BY-CONSTRUCTION: make an invalid decomposition (nearly) impossible to emit *(2026-07-02, user — HIGH-PRIORITY, "invest a lot of effort")*
> **User framing (2026-07-02):** *"the decompose part should be designed in a way so that the model cannot really produce invalid graphs … at least boil it down to some approach that leads to valid graphs. This is gonna be a KEY part of whether !Klein can thrive or crawls in the mud … invest 'a lot of effort' into getting this right."* This is a **make-or-break** capability: the decomposition graph is the spine of every swarm run — a bad graph either dead-locks the board or produces incoherent work. Treat it with the depth we gave the §5.AA robustness ladder.
>
> **WHY NOW (live-found 2026-07-02):** driving `complex_dag` through the fleet, the 120B architect (gpt-oss-120b) emitted a graph where **every** card had a dependency — including a `doc-domain-model ↔ classify-score-bands` 2-cycle — so `rootTaskIds` was empty and the cascade **never started** (12 cards frozen in planning). We shipped a **REPAIR** safety net (`breakDependencyCycles`, commit 43f32d31 — deterministic back-edge removal at apply time so there is always a startable root). **But repair ≠ prevention.** The bet here is to move validity UPSTREAM so the model *cannot easily* emit a broken graph in the first place — repair stays only as the last-resort net. Related failure modes already seen: cyclic deps (this), over-constrained "no root" graphs, disconnected/orphan test&docs cards (§5's `assessNKleinPlanTaskGraphQuality`), single-giant-card non-decompositions, and cards that "complete" without delivering (the single-card PARTIAL — a different axis).
>
> **DEEP-RESEARCH MANDATE (do this before committing to a design — a lot of effort is authorized):** run a broad, cited investigation (`/deep-research` or a Workflow research sweep) across ALL of:
- [x] **Constrained / structured generation** — grammar-constrained decoding (GBNF/llama.cpp, XGrammar, Outlines, LMQL, Guidance, `jsonschemabender`), and whether a **DAG-shaped grammar** can make cycles/dangling-refs *unrepresentable* at decode time. NB reasoning-model incompatibility already found (§5.AN: `json_schema` dead-ends on the resident reasoning tier → native tool-call wrapper instead) — so a grammar approach must be reasoning-aware. *(SHIPPED 2026-07-05: incremental-dag-construction.ts (14 tests))*
- [~] **Incremental construction protocols** — emit the graph via a **sequence of validated tool calls** (`add_task`, `add_dependency` with a per-call acyclicity + reference check that REJECTS the bad edge and tells the model why) instead of one-shot whole-graph emission. Topological-insertion invariant: a new edge may only point at an already-declared earlier node ⇒ acyclic by construction. Compare one-shot-then-validate vs incremental-validated for weak local models (which loop when bounced — see `deriveOpenQuestionDefaults`). **PURE CORE SHIPPED (2026-07-05): [src/core/incremental-dag-construction.ts](src/core/incremental-dag-construction.ts)** — the valid-by-construction state machine (design direction (1)). `applyDagOp(state, op)` validates each add_node/add_edge against the partial graph: rejects empty/duplicate ids, dangling edges (reference check), self-loops, duplicate edges, and any edge that would close a cycle (reachability: reject from→to iff `from` already reachable from `to`) — a rejected op leaves state UNCHANGED and returns a stable reason + a model-facing `message` (the 'tell it why' feedback the runtime relays so a weak model fixes the ONE bad edge, not the whole graph). PROVEN invariant: after ANY op sequence, `scoreValidDag(dagConstructionToGraph(state)) === 1`. `applyDagOps` folds a sequence + returns the per-op trace; composes with the §5.AB scorer's TaskGraph. 14 tests. **REMAINING:** (a) runtime wiring — expose add_task/add_dependency as decompose tools whose handlers call applyDagOp + relay the reject message into the tool-loop (hot path, do with a live chat-e2e); (b) the weak-vs-strong fleet COMPARISON (one-shot+repair vs incremental-validated) via the §5.AB eval harness — measure before/after, don't guess.
- [~] **Scientific / graph theory** — DAG construction & repair, minimum feedback-arc-set (optimal cycle-breaking vs our greedy DFS), topological sort as a generation constraint, SCC condensation, graph grammars / hyperedge replacement.
      *(PREMISE PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-07-08: the "greedy DFS" baseline this compares against no longer exists — `breakDependencyCycles`
      ([plan-task-cycle-break.ts](src/nklein-agent/decomposition/plan-task-cycle-break.ts)) already moved to **SCC-CONDENSE** (Tarjan → sequential
      chain in emission order), a research-corrected choice (audit 2026-07-02 §5.AV) that DELIBERATELY preserves the architect's coupling instead
      of doing min-FAS "remove the fewest edges." So min-feedback-arc-set is NOT a drop-in improvement here — it optimizes a different objective
      (fewest edges cut) than the shipped design (preserve tight-coupling as an ordered chain); adopting it would REGRESS the coupling-preservation
      intent. Topological-sort-as-generation-constraint + SCC-condensation are BOTH already applied (incremental-dag-construction.ts §5.AV 9842 +
      this repair). Remaining genuinely-open research: graph-grammars / hyperedge-replacement for a DAG-shaped decode grammar — but §5.AN already
      found GBNF is a no-op on LM Studio (only json_schema/native-tool work), so a decode-time DAG grammar is not viable on the current runtime.
      Net: the actionable graph-theory levers are shipped; this stays a research pointer, not an implementation leaf.)*
- [ ] **Project-management decomposition theory** — Work Breakdown Structure (WBS 100%-rule, mutually-exclusive/collectively-exhaustive), PERT/CPM & critical path, **Design/Dependency Structure Matrix (DSM)** and its tearing/partitioning algorithms (a mature "make the dependency matrix acyclic" body of work directly applicable here), story-mapping / vertical-slice decomposition.

### 5.AW — EAGER fleet utilization: no LLM idles while it can add value *(2026-07-02, user — HIGH-PRIORITY)*
> **STATUS (2026-07-05): a DESIGN/PRINCIPLE section — its executable slices are BUILT AS LEAVES elsewhere, not orphaned
> here.** The opportunistic-work scheduler = the durable-scheduler wiring tracked in §5.AS/§5.AF (STEP 2-3); family-diverse
> routing = §5.AB; the strong-model idle picker (`memory_audit` / `opportunistic-idle-work`) already SHIPPED (§5.AR note).
> This section is the value-ladder + N-eyes-with-orthogonal-lenses PRINCIPLE those leaves must honor; it carries no
> ready leaf of its own (its 2 open decisions — speculative best-of-N aggressiveness + a per-run compute ceiling — ride
> the §5.AB/§5.AW `[?]` user-questions, some already resolved per [[decisions-and-scope-2026-07-04]]).
> **User framing (2026-07-02):** *"implement measures so we avoid LLMs idling … no need to let 120b idle while 4b is coding … no llm shall idle if there is anything VALUABLE possible to assign to it … we don't want lazy agents, they shall be EAGER to contribute wherever they can add value."* The fleet is expensive resident capacity; leaving a strong model idle while another grinds is pure waste. Ties [[fleet-throughput-sweet-spots]] (m5max is a farm; the 120B is the FASTEST model at 85 tok/s — idling it is the worst waste) + §5.AB (routing) + the swarm-behavior audit (compute-efficiency · review-modelling · deliberation).
>
> **THE KEY INSIGHT — idle models default to READ-ONLY, NO-CONFLICT value work.** Why cards serialize today: the file-overlap guard blocks two cards touching the same files (correct — avoids merge conflicts). But REVIEW / VERIFY / DELIBERATE / CONTEXT-PREP touch NO workspace files, so they are ALWAYS safe to assign to an idle model in parallel. So an idle 120B while a 4B codes should be **reviewing/verifying that work (a diverse second opinion — §5.AB), deliberating a pending hard decision (§5.AW ties the deliberation feature), or prepping context for upcoming cards** — turning idle time directly into quality + throughput. This unifies "no idle" with reasoning-diversity (the idle large model IS the diverse critic).
>
> **Opportunistic-work value ladder (assign the HIGHEST-value available task to a going-idle model; "valuable" is the gate — never busy-work):**
> 1. **Work-ahead** — start the next dependency-ready card that does NOT file-overlap an active one (extends the cascade; already partly there, make it eager up to the fleet's real free capacity, not a static cap).
> 2. **Review / verify** — a capable idle model reviews a just-finished card (prefer a DIFFERENT family than the author → uncorrelated judgment) or runs the acceptance gate. Read-only ⇒ always parallel-safe.
> 3. **Deliberate** — join/seed a discussion on a pending hard/ambiguous decision (decompose choice, conflicting review, architecture) — see the deliberation design (swarm-behavior audit).
> 4. **Speculative exploration** — best-of-N on a known-hard card (a diverse model tries an alternative approach in its own sandbox; keep the best), or pre-decompose an upcoming stream.
> 5. **Context / knowledge prep** — build the repo-map/embeddings/index for upcoming cards (§5.AR codebase-memory), refresh retrieval (§5.AC), mine the ledger (§5.AF) to improve the catalog.
>
> **MECHANISM (to design + build):** an **opportunistic-work scheduler** — when a model endpoint goes idle (own-sessions + `lms ps` busy-state), pick the highest-value SAFE task for it from the ladder, gated by: value (skip if nothing genuinely useful), per-machine concurrency + memory (don't oversubscribe — see the m4mini incident, [[dont-churn-user-managed-machines]]), no file-overlap for write tasks, and a token/compute budget (eager ≠ wasteful — bounded speculative work). Prefer assigning REVIEW/DELIBERATE to strong idle models (best ROI), WORK-AHEAD to fast coders. Record every opportunistic assignment + its value outcome to the ledger so the scheduler learns what actually pays off.
>
> **★ N-EYES WITH ORTHOGONAL PERSPECTIVES (user 2026-07-02 — the refinement that makes eager review VALUABLE, not redundant):** *"4-eyes ramped up to as many eyes as we have available … while making sure to not just waste compute … second, third, fourth eyes must take EXTENDED/ADAPTED perspectives so we really generate value and not iterate the same insight all over again."* The failure mode to design against: N models given the same generic "review this" prompt largely re-derive the SAME top findings (redundancy ≠ value). Design:
> - **Assigned LENSES, not accidental overlap.** Each additional eye gets a DISTINCT, explicit perspective: correctness/spec-fit → edge-cases/robustness → security/injection/isolation → integration/composability (does it fit the neighboring cards' work? — the missing cross-card review) → performance → test-quality (do the tests actually pin the behavior?) → simplicity/maintainability → user-intent ("is this what was ASKED?"). Lens order ≈ value order; a 2-eye card gets the top 2 lenses, a hard card gets more.
> - **Diversity on BOTH axes:** model FAMILY diversity (uncorrelated priors — §5.AB) × PERSPECTIVE diversity (uncorrelated focus). Prefer assigning each lens to a family whose strengths match (security lens → strongest reasoner; test-quality → a coder family).
> - **Blind-then-confer:** first pass BLIND (each eye reviews independently — avoids anchoring on the first reviewer's frame), then a cheap CONFER step: later eyes see prior findings ONLY to (a) dedupe, (b) EXTEND ("what did they miss given my lens?"), (c) dispute — conflicts escalate to the deliberation mechanism (a diverse judge resolves). Never show a later eye the prior findings BEFORE its own blind pass.
> - **Marginal-value stopping rule:** track NEW-findings-per-eye; when an eye adds nothing non-duplicate, STOP adding eyes (dry-run rule). Record per-lens/per-family yield to the §5.AF ledger so the scheduler LEARNS how many eyes + which lenses each card type actually deserves (difficulty-scaled: trivial card = 1 eye; risky/hard = the full panel).
> - **Same principle for DELIBERATION:** discussion participants get assigned STANCES/angles (risk-first vs simplicity-first vs user-first), not N copies of "what do you think?".
>
> **Guardrails / open tensions:** (a) "valuable" must be real — a completeness/value check before assigning, else agents do noise; (b) speculative best-of-N burns compute — gate on card difficulty + a budget; (c) idle-review must not deadlock (review of a card whose author is still running = review the WIP snapshot or wait for awaiting_review); (d) local-only + memory-safe (respect the guardrails). **USER QUESTIONS:** how aggressive should speculative best-of-N be (off by default? only for cards flagged hard?), and is there a compute/token budget ceiling per run the eager-scheduler must stay under? Converges with §5.AB · §5.AA · §5.AF (ledger/durable lease) · the deliberation + compute-efficiency audits.

## 7. Success criteria (the bar for "done")
1. Cloud is unreachable; a cloud-pinned card hard-stops; re-enabling is one reviewed code change.
2. No oversized prompt ever leaves; over-budget turns compact or stop.
3. The loop is stable: no 1s timeouts, no restart-config failures, no retry storms.
4. ≥32k enforced everywhere; budgets/compression scale to the local window with no hardcoded constants.
5. A multi-card DAG auto-starts unblocked cards under the cap, serializes per endpoint, parallelizes across
   endpoints, never thrashes the machine.
6. **A single high-level prompt yields a Planning-lane DAG of local-feasible cards that get created and flow
   into execution — with strict isolation ON.** *(DAG-under-isolation + a started card verified; fully-automatic
   unblocked-card swarm start is the remaining end-to-end target.)*
7. Context is a segmented green→red bar against the real effective window.
8. Parallel cards never collide on shared files; result-branches merge in dependency order; runs are budgeted,
   one-click stoppable, stalled tasks auto-park.
9. The board is a live cockpit (per-agent status, MCSR, DAG + fit badges, diagnostics, first-run wizard) — all
   cloud-free.
10. A loose idea triggers clarifying questions, yields a reviewable plain-language plan, adapts on
    execution-discovered gaps.
11. Nothing built since branching from `main` is invisible in the UI (coverage matrix has no unmapped entry).
12. **Every agent shell/FS action runs in Docker; no host fallback; Docker-down fails closed.**
13. Upstream-clean: re-pulling the SDK contracts needs no reverts.

---

## 8. Superseded decisions & direction changes (history — so nothing is lost or re-litigated)

- **Cloud went from "normal option" → banned.** The original `plan.md` targeted 8–16k small models and treated
  cloud as always-available. One day of telemetry showed cloud defaulting to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` and
  causing 678× "Insufficient balance", 227× "1.1M-token prompt exceeds 1M limit", 227× "1s timeout", 453×
  "No previous session config". Result: **LOCAL ONLY + ≥32k minimum** invariants (§1). All cloud paths are
  hidden/parked, not deleted, so a future single-file re-enable is possible.
- **Host worktrees → Docker clone-in/patch-out.** The early model ran agent tools on host task worktrees; replaced
  by **strict Docker isolation** with `nklein/tasks/<task>` result branches applied host-side. The worktree
  **creation** machinery is now retired (§5.A, 2026-06-23) — no live nklein path creates or reads a worktree; only
  legacy on-disk *cleanup* + the dead terminal-CLI-agent scaffolding remain (C7d/C7e/C8 + verification left).
- **Decomposition under isolation was briefly dark, then restored.** For a period, sandboxed planning omitted
  `decompose_project`/`expand_task`. Decision reversed 2026-06-19: they are *trusted control-plane* and stay
  host-side (they touch only plan artifacts + the board). The earlier "produce a plan in chat instead of
  /kanban-decompose" guidance is superseded.
- **Portable-state conflict model = CRDT** (not last-writer-wins-with-manual-rebase). Chosen 2026-06-21; merge
  is automatic, so no manual rebase UI is needed.
- **New direction (postdates the planning chain): grow !Klein's own core.** A local-only Python core sidecar
  (`core-py/`) and a TS native agent core (`src/agent-core/`) now provide ML + native-agent capabilities the
  vendored SDK can't (constrained/grammar decoding, own embeddings/compression/repomap, native ReAct loop). The
  vendored SDK remains one supported runtime, no longer the only one (§5.H, §6.10).
- **SDK is now vendored & de-packaged in-repo** (§6.12) — the `@nkleinbot/*` "never patch node_modules" framing
  from the predecessor docs is updated: the SDK lives under `vendor/nklein-sdk/` and is ours to edit; the
  boundary discipline (`check:nklein-boundary`, `src/nklein-agent/` plug-ins) still holds for *integration*.
- **Archival sources (folded in, then deleted):** `follow-up-1..4.md` + `findings-from-follow-up-work-4.md` were
  already declared archival by the iteration playbook — their open items live on as §5.A (isolation/worktree)
  and §5.A (UI verification); their shipped items are in §6. `follow-up-5.md`/`follow-up-6.md` open threads are
  §5.A–§5.F. `specsheet.md`/`plan.md` status is reconciled into §6 (shipped) and §5 (open). All are superseded
  by **this file**.

## 9. Changelog discipline
`CHANGELOG.md` is **release notes**, not a work log (pre-version: branched off `main`, no released version yet, no
back-compat burden). Record only **features / user-facing behavior changes** since the last version, plus **fixes for
bugs that already existed on `main`** — derived from the real diff, within the same change. Do **NOT** log bugs we
introduce *and* fix during this pre-version phase (they never shipped); fix them with a test only. Resume normal
"every fix" discipline once a version is released. Only open a PR / cut a release when the user asks.
